newsitem.title: NORWAY: ALPINE SKIING-DOWNHILL INTERRUPTED WITH KJUS IN LEAD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-DOWNHILL INTERRUPTED WITH KJUS IN LEAD.

text.p: Norway's Lasse Kjus was leading a men's Alpine ski World Cup downhill on Saturday when the race was called to a halt after 29 skiers because of high winds.

Kjus, taking advantage of a brief lull in the conditions, rocketed down the 2,641-metre Olympiabakken course in a time of one minute 28.07 seconds, almost one second faster than Austria's Patrick Ortlieb who was lying second with 1:29.03.
Canada's Ed Podivinsky, who claimed a bronze medal on the same course at the 1992 Olympics, was third quickest in 1:29.19.
Organisers attempted to get one more skier down the windswept course in order to make the race official but the gusting winds prevented any further racing.
Under International Ski Federation (FIS) rules, 30 skiers needed to have started to make the results stand automatically.
Officials were meeting to decide whether to declare the results official.
